title: Adaptive Pricing Bands & Attribution Overlay — UX prototype for token-level cost scenarios
creator: Samantha Kim
description: Goal: Design a compact, inspectable UI pattern that lets product and finance users build, compare, and export token-level pricing scenarios aligned to actual usage attribution. The feature combines: 1) adaptive pricing bands (user-defined or suggested price breaks) mapped to token buckets; 2) an attribution overlay that shows which prompts/messages/rules contributed to each cost band; 3) an export flow (CSV + nested JSON) for downstream billing and forecasting. This ticket covers exploratory prototypes, edge-case decisions, and a handoff-ready spec for engineering.
acceptance_criteria: Design files (Figma) with 3 responsive states: compact list, waterfall detail, and attribution overlay
Prototype demonstrates toggling between cost bands and underlying attribution traces within 2 clicks
Export exports role-aware CSV and optional nested JSON payload with stable schema and example payload included
Performance constraints and sampling behavior documented for >100k daily messages
Design handoff includes tokenization rules, aggregation windows, and privacy notes for PII-sensitive prompts
design_notes: We prioritize clarity over raw token granularity for large accounts. The UI shows sampled per-prompt attribution when full per-token lineage would be too noisy or expensive to compute. Default 'Suggested Bands' are computed by the Optimize service; user can create custom bands. Attribution overlay floats over any chart and is anchored to series points. Export must be filterable by role and date range. We considered inline per-token drilldown (too heavy) and so settled on a hybrid: per-message lineage with optional sample-rate field.

implementation_notes: Engineering needs: 1) API endpoint for band definitions and suggested bands from Optimize; 2) aggregation endpoint that returns per-band totals plus sampled attribution traces; 3) export endpoint that streams CSV/JSON with schema v1. Include query params: start_ts, end_ts, route_id, model_version, role_filter, sample_rate. Suggest retention: store full lineage for 30 days, sampled lineage for 90 days. Documented trade-off: lower sample_rate reduces cost but may lower attribution fidelity.
decision_log: 2026-03-03: Rejected full per-token export due to cost. Decided on per-message sampled lineage with sample_rate field.
2026-03-06: Agreed to add admin-only 'Export raw prompts' toggle behind RBAC and audit logging.
2026-03-09: Opted for three visual modes (compact, waterfall, overlay) to support both finance and developer audiences.
